reason: The conclusion stands: take no action and follow R41-A3, which was logged before the read. R41-A3 says it keys 'late' and T8 on the poller header as logged, which supersedes the L_hi keying of R38-A5. The builder does exactly that: in mk_card_1837.py (sha8 a19e1bd6) l.49, late = (hdr - T0) > 10.2 h, and the guard uses base <= / > 10.75 h. One claim in the finding is wrong, though. The disagreement windows depend on F: they are (edge - 210 s x F, edge]. lb_poll.py makes at most 3 attempts, so a block that carries data has F <= 2. For F = 2 the windows are (19:05:17, 19:12:17] and (19:38:17, 19:45:17]. The projected header 19:05:28Z therefore falls inside the F=2 late window, with an 11 s margin. That case still does not change the decision. Both T1 and T2 promote at display >= 0.960, and under decision B 0.959 is T3KEEP either way. Only the UNPROVEN-ins clause, or the T5 'DIS «?»' text, would differ. The 19:35:35Z header sits 2:42 outside the F=2 T8 window. The 19:45:37Z header is past the edge in both keyings, so it is T8 either way. manual_admit.sh makes a single attempt, so F is always 0 there. The chance of hitting this is also small. Only 3 of 579 data-carrying poll.log blocks had F >= 1 (2 had F = 2). Failed attempts actually cost about 32 s each (F=3 blocks shift the next header by 694-701 s against about 602 s), far below the 210 s bound, so the header keying is closer to the truth anyway. There is no value or feasibility issue, because nothing gets built or submitted.
